Position Title: Commissioning Project Manager

Position Location: Remote – United States. Must be located near a major airport.

Travel Requirements: Up to 50% domestic travel. Must have a valid driver’s license and ability to rent vehicles.

JOB SUMMARY

The Commissioning Project Manager provides technical support and leadership to plan, schedule and execute full life cycle commissioning of critical facilities. This person participates in the MEP design review process and participates in functional testing of complex electrical and mechanical systems.

The Commissioning Project Manager is responsible for supporting all aspects of a project. This person will work as part of the project team and interact closely with the owners, designers, contractors, subcontractors and other trades on projects in mission critical environments.

The role may assist with developing and evaluating bid proposals, developing commissioning plans and schedules, facilitating communication and ensuring compliance with owner’s requirements, applicable laws, and specifications.

This person will collaborate with design engineers, construction contractors, equipment vendors, client staff and the DLB commissioning team to test, validate and make operational newly installed and operational electrical and mechanical systems including those in mission critical facilities.

The Commissioning Project Manager will receive limited directions on day-to-day work and general instruction on new projects or assignments. Will execute commissioning and assist project leadership on projects of complex scope. Will work independently or under limited supervision.

This person will communicate and operate in line with organizational goals and values, as well as departmental objectives.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Manage all Elements of Commissioning Projects (50%)

  • Assist with pre-construction elements including project initiation, kickoff, RFIs and submittals
  • Coordinate and support resource and material forecasting
  • Develop, manage and monitor schedule
  • Participate in, schedule or lead project meetings
  • Coordinate / perform QA / QC and Cx plans and specifications to ensure completion in accordance with the project scope and appropriate guidelines and manuals
  • Communicate and coordinate project staffing needs.
  • Coordinate or oversee start-up, cutover, pre-functional or functional testing and project closeout
  • Onboard project team for mobilization
  • Prepare project progress reports for internal and external stakeholders
  • Lead and assist in preparation of final commissioning report for submission to client

Monitor and Control Project Financials (15%)

  • Prepare, forecast and monitor project budgets, profitability, margins, bill rates and utilization and maintain overall responsibility for the profitability of the project
  • Communicate with the client when additional fees / change orders are required
  • Identify potential project risks and develop / implement strategies to minimize impact and control deviations from estimated costs and project deadlines

Manage Stakeholder Relations (15%)

  • Assist in the preparation of proposals, presentations and the overall marketing efforts of the firm
  • Assist in the promotion of the firm, service and expertise to existing or potential clients
  • Maintain client relationship to ensure an ongoing positive relationship and work with clients to identify and develop new projects
  • Support contact for clients and build effective, long-term client relationships
  • Ensure client satisfaction through active communication

Perform On-site Commissioning Activities (10%)

  • On-site inspection, validation, functional testing, verification and troubleshooting of electrical and mechanical equipment
  • Participate in factory witness testing and observe startup activities
  • Use technical equipment to perform testing
  • Direct vendors / contractors in the execution of the testing

Develop Testing Plans and Procedures for Complex Projects (5%)

  • Development of commissioning plans
  • Prepare pre-functional checklists
  • Prepare functional performance test scripts

Review Construction Related Design Documents, Drawings and Specifications (5%)

  • Review shop drawings and submittals
  • Review sequence of operations
  • Assist in commissioning focused design reviews

Completion of Assigned Tasks and Deliverables on Time and on Budget

Performs Other Related Duties as Assigned

POSITION REQUIREMENTS (INTERMEDIATE LEVEL FOR ALL THE FOLLOWING EXCEPT AS NOTED)

  • Knowledge of industry trends, project management and construction procedures and best practices
  • Knowledge of business and management principles involved in strategic planning, resource allocation, leadership technique, and coordination of people and resources
  • Knowledge of materials, methods, and the tools involved in the construction mission critical, commercial buildings, or other structures
  • Skilled in completing assignments accurately and with attention to detail
  • Skilled at managing personnel and material resources
  • Ability to leverage AI and emerging technologies to streamline workflows, optimize operational processes, and contribute to company-wide innovation.
  • Ability to work successfully in a remote environment through effective communication and organizational skills, self-motivation, proactiveness and resourcefulness in a distraction free workspace
  • Ability to learn client and / or industry specific management software
  • Ability to follow company and site safety requirements
  • Ability to analyze and prepare documents, reports, and correspondence
  • Ability to communicate effectively in both oral and written form (technical and non-technical information)
  • Ability to communicate effectively directly with clients and at times serve as primary point of client contact
  • Ability to work successfully as a member of a team and independently with moderate supervision
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively with onsite and remote team members
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet close deadlines
  • Ability to effectively plan and delegate the work of others
  • Ability to analyze complex information and develop plans to address identified issues
  • Proficient at using MS Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams), along with exceptional organizational skills for file management
  • Organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The following physical demands must be met by the employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is

  • Frequently manipulating, moving or grasping small parts, devices or tools

Position Overview

Insurance Verification

Verify patient insurance after the patient checks in, typically around 15 minutes after the scheduled appointment time. Ensure all insurance information is accurate, updated, and properly documented.

Denied Claims Management

Review denied claims, identify denial reasons, and assist with claim reprocessing. Track issues, follow up on missing information, and help prevent repeat claim errors.

EOB Processing

Review and process Explanation of Benefits documents. Help organize, validate, and clear EOB backlogs while ensuring billing and insurance documentation is accurate.

Patient Balance Resolution

Review outstanding insurance balances and patient account issues. Track unresolved balances, identify the source of the issue, and coordinate next steps for resolution.

Claims Processing

Support claims-related workflows, including Cigna and Veterans Affairs claims. Ensure claims are reviewed, tracked, and escalated when necessary.

Payment Coordination

Assist with vendor payment coordination, including check payments when needed. Ensure payment-related tasks are completed accurately and on time.

SOAP Note Monitoring

Monitor SOAP note completion, accuracy, and compliance. Track missing, incomplete, or delayed documentation and communicate concerns appropriately.

Appointment Tracking

Track missed appointments, canceled appointments, and scheduling trends. Identify patterns that may affect clinic revenue, patient flow, or provider productivity.

Reports and Operational Tracking

Prepare reports on outstanding balances, missed appointments, canceled appointments, EOB backlog, denied claims, and other operational metrics. Reports should include clear insights and practical recommendations when needed.

Team Coordination

Support smooth communication between the provider, care team, and administrative staff. Help ensure updates are clearly shared, priorities are followed through, and important tasks are not missed.

Operational Support

Proactively identify workflow gaps, billing concerns, documentation delays, scheduling issues, and patient account problems. Recommend practical solutions to improve clinic efficiency.

  • Minimum of 1 year of experience as a Medical Virtual Assistant

  • Experience supporting a US healthcare practice

  • Experience with insurance verification, EOBs, claims, denied claims, patient balances, or billing support

  • Exposure to CPT and ICD-10 codes

  • Strong English communication skills, both written and verbal

  • Strong attention to detail and follow-through

  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision

Required Soft Skills

  • Proactive and able to anticipate needs before being asked

  • Highly detail-oriented with billing, documentation, and reporting tasks

  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills

  • Emotionally intelligent and patient when working with a busy provider

  • Able to take personal responsibility for assigned work

  • Resourceful and self-motivated when learning new workflows

Global Citizen’s PR & Communications department is seeking a dynamic PR professional with a passion for innovative storytelling, sharp news sense, and a strong contact list of industry-leading journalists across Europe, the Middle East and Africa to help further Global Citizen’s mission to end extreme poverty and drive positive impact globally.

Reporting to the VP of PR & Communications, the objective of the Director, Public Relations & Communications, EMEA, is to protect and promote Global Citizen’s brand in Europe, the Middle East and Africa. This is done through proactive and thoughtful sourcing and pitching of news from and for the organization, and building and maintaining a network of journalists and social influencers to which these stories can be shared with. This role will lead on outreach and maintaining relationships with journalists in the above key markets with tier-1 outlets and platforms, formulating innovative and timely pitches that elevate Global Citizen’s campaigns, events and executive spokespeople to new and existing audiences across sectors. The Director, Public Relations & Communications EMEA will develop and execute PR strategies for priority initiatives in close coordination with the New York office, including the Artist Relations, Marketing, Brand Partnerships and Global Policy & Advocacy departments, with support from external PR agencies in Africa and Abu Dhabi.

jobs.description:
350.org is seeking a senior consultant on Audience Growth on Social Media to deliver content production targeting US audiences within our global social media channels, with a focus on measurable audience growth across our shared global platforms. This is a temporary, results-oriented assignment.

The consultant is a senior professional with demonstrated expertise across the full social media lifecycle: strategic planning, performance evaluation, and content production – as well as hands-on experience setting up and optimizing awareness and growth advertising campaigns.

The Global Communications Director is the contract manager and is responsible for approving deliverables and authorizing invoices. The Consultant will participate in agreed fortnightly progress reviews.

  • Commitment: The assignment is estimated at approximately 100 full-time consultant days during the period of 6 months, invoiced monthly against deliverable progress.
  • Location: Remote within the United States, preferably in EST timezone.
  • Hourly rate: $49.15

Scope of Work

Deliverables:

  • An audience growth plan and its execution for 350.org's global social media channels (Instagram and Facebook) among US-based audiences, aligned with the KPI targets outlined below.
  • A dedicated growth project for the 350 Action US Instagram account, aimed at reaching the 10,000-follower target outlined below.
  • At least one message-testing project focused on energy affordability, connected to and informing the Great Power Shift campaign.
  • A final set of recommendations, delivered by the end of the contract, covering: priority audience segments, key messages to prioritize going forward, and practices to continue, based on data and insights gathered throughout the assignment.

Key Performance Indicators:

  • Growth of 20% in the US-based following of 350.org's global Instagram and Facebook pages, especially within the age segment of 25 - 45 years old.
  • Growth of the 350 Action US account to 10,000 followers.
  • Increased engagement rate (likes, comments, shares, saves, video views, click-through rate on Linktree and petition links) among US-focused posts on global pages.
  • Improved conversion rate on calls-to-action (e.g., petition sign-ups, sign-ups via Linktree) attributable to US-targeted content and advertising.
  • Benchmarking will be conducted at the start of the assignment.

Main Duties include:

Strategy and Content Localization:

  • Develop and execute a US-audience social media growth strategy aligned with global campaign priorities and organizational KPIs.
  • Adapt global campaign narratives, key messages, and creative assets for US audiences, calibrating tone, cultural framing, and format while maintaining brand consistency with the organization's global voice.
  • Produce at least 15 content pieces per month across all channels, including short-form video, copy, and visual content optimized for US audiences, applying platform-specific best practices (aspect ratios, captioning, hook structure, posting cadence, content trends) for distribution across the organization's global Instagram and Facebook channels, as well as the 350 Action US account.
  • Develop a content review protocol, with criteria and workflow for assessing incoming global content for risk of underperformance or cultural misalignment with US audiences. Apply the protocol to review each piece of content as it comes in (approximately 5 pieces per week), providing feedback within 24 hours of submission.
  • Coordinate with global communications colleagues on audience segmentation, content production, and publishing schedules. Apply geolocation and audience segmentation protocols when publishing US-specific content, to preserve relevance for non-US followers on shared global channels.
  • Liaise with Digital Engagement and Global Social Media colleagues to localize and adapt CTAs for the US audience context.

Audience Insight and Evaluation:

  • Analyze engagement and growth metrics for US-based followers (including reach, impressions, engagement rate, follower growth rate, and audience retention) using platform analytics and social listening tools. Submit findings and recommendations to the Global Social Media team.
  • Deliver proactive and timely content strategy recommendations and outputs, based on ongoing monitoring of US cultural discourse, platform algorithm updates, creative trends, and emerging social/media narratives.
  • Design and interpret A/B and message testing protocols targeted at US audiences, using statistically sound sample sizes and control variables.
  • Track performance against growth KPIs and iterate tactics based on data analysis.

Advertising:

  • Set up, manage, and evaluate paid awareness and growth advertising campaigns (e.g. Meta Ads) to support follower growth objectives.
  • Optimize ad targeting parameters, budget allocation, bidding strategy, and creative assets based on performance metrics including CPM, CPC, CTR, conversion rate, and ROAS (return on ad spend).
  • Monitor cost-efficiency indicators (CPA, cost-per-follower) and advise budget allocation across campaigns/ad sets to maximize return on investment, with approval from the Global Communications Director.

Crisis Communication:

  • Support the global communications team in developing and executing crisis communication protocols relevant to US audiences and platforms.
  • Monitor for reputational risk indicators or fast-moving situations requiring rapid-response content.

Qualifications and Experience:

Required:

  • Senior-level experience in social media strategy, with a demonstrated track record of driving measurable audience growth.
  • Tech-savvy, with proven experience adapting content and strategy to platform algorithm changes and evolving creative trends, leveraging these shifts to drive performance improvements.
  • Hands-on experience creating and publishing content for Instagram and Facebook, including copy, graphics, and short-form video production. Proficiency with Canva.
  • Experience setting up, managing, and evaluating paid social advertising campaigns, with fluency in core performance metrics (CPM, CTR, CPA, ROAS, conversion rate).
  • Proficiency with audience insight and social listening tools (e.g. Google Trends/Insights, Junkipedia, Brandwatch or similar) to inform content and strategic decisions.
  • Proven senior experience in crisis communication and rapid response situations.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to translate performance data into actionable strategy and concrete content outputs.
  • Strong writing skills in English, with demonstrated ability to adapt tone and voice across audience segments.

Desirable:

  • Experience with advocacy, campaigning, or nonprofit communications.
  • Spanish as a secondary language.

jobs.description:
Remote with Required On-Site Presence in Los Angeles (April 4th - 6th, 2026)

Bully Pulpit International is an outcomes agency made up of strategists, data scientists, and artists. We come from politics, brands, and government and we communicate without barriers and measure what matters. We have more than 400 team members in six countries and thirteen offices — Berlin, Brussels, Chicago, D.C., London, Los Angeles, New York, Oslo, San Francisco, and Zürich. We apply our unique expertise across strategic communications, public affairs, research, and digital marketing to create sophisticated and customized strategies that make change possible for both American and European clients.

About the Convening:

A Day of Unreasonable Conversation (UC) is an invitation-only annual summit which serves as a

trusted, curated space designed to foster honest, nuanced, and critical discourse on the most urgent

issues of our time. The gathering bridges the gap between the entertainment industry and social

impact sectors. It connects "culture shapers"—influential television writers, showrunners, producers,

executives, and digital storytellers who are literally writing the script for the world—with frontline

changemakers, advocates, philanthropists, and issue experts.

The core mission of UC is to "unlock progress through the power of stories". In a deeply polarized

moment where trust in traditional media is at a record low, the event aims to spark writers' rooms with

new ideas and give creators the tools to drive meaningful change. UC challenges storytellers to

complicate the narrative by moving beyond flat tropes and oversimplified binaries to explore the

systemic complexities of our time. Ultimately, the goal is to bring greater nuance, empathy, and truth to

the stories that shape public perception.

UC is grounded in the belief that culture is the multiplier for change at scale. Because culture sits

upstream of policy and politics, it is where people already are. Even in times of deep fracture when

people stop listening to experts or political parties, they still listen to stories. By bringing storytellers and

problem-solvers together, UC seeks to turn stage-side insights into long-term creative collaborations

that shift culture on screen and beyond.

A Day of Unreasonable Conversation is founded and produced by the social impact agency Propper

Daley x Bully Pulpit International (BPI). The event relies on cross-sector collaboration and is fully funded

by philanthropy.

Requirements

We’re hiring a Senior Director of Audience & Community, reporting directly to the Executive Director, to build and steward the community at the heart of A Day of Unreasonable Conversation. This person will own the full audience function—from strategy and curation through CRM, outreach, guest experience, day-of execution, and long-term relationship building. We’re looking for someone who sees the audience as a strategic asset and a living network, not a static guest list, and who can build and run this function with real authority and minimal oversight.

While the Day of Unreasonable Conversation is the community's annual gathering, this role is also responsible for activating that community throughout the year through small convenings (Evenings of Unreasonable Conversations), fellowships, editorial touchpoints, and ongoing relationship stewardship that keeps people connected between convenings.

Curation matters as much as headcount. We want a room with genuine diversity across perspectives, creative backgrounds, and positions in the industry. That means thinking carefully about what each person’s pr

What You’ll Do

Strategy & Curation

  • Own the audience composition strategy. Curate a room of approximately 500 guests that brings together the entertainment industry and the social impact sector. The audience should reflect both the trusted relationships UC has built over time and the creators, executives, organizations, and changemakers whose work is most relevant to the cultural conversation in the year of the convening. Every year’s room should feel intentional, current, and additive.
    • Lead the audience strategy for three Evenings of Unreasonable Conversations, curating intimate gatherings that introduce new voices, deepen relationships within the existing community, and intentionally funnel participants into the annual Day of Unreasonable Conversation.
  • Entertainment side: Writers and showrunners, producers and directors, network and studio executives who greenlight content, digital creators and online storytellers reflecting how culture is created and distributed today, and industry gatekeepers including agents, managers, and publicists—who shape which stories and talent reach audiences.
  • Social impact side: Frontline activists, researchers, policy experts, nonprofit and foundation leaders, and people with lived experience who bring subject-matter expertise and real-world perspective into the room.
  • Own audience strategy beyond “filling the room.” Build a year-round community, not a one-day guest list. Define the audience function as a pipeline into fellowships, future convenings, and ongoing engagement, with clear goals for room composition, ideological and sector diversity, cultural influence, and long-term relationship building.
  • Build and maintain the ecosystem map. Create and steward a living map of aligned organizations (studios, networks, production companies, nonprofits, advocacy groups, foundations, agencies, etc.), maintaining relationships throughout the year so UC is continuously expanding and strengthening its community rather than rebuilding it each event cycle.
  • Develop audience engagement strategies for different community segments, including returning attendees, fellows, funders, creative leaders, first-time participants, and strategic partners, ensuring each group has meaningful opportunities to engage with UC throughout the year.
  • Run a tiered outreach and room-design strategy. Execute a Tier 1/2/3 invitation rollout against defined room-mix targets by sector, geography, ideology, influence, and creative discipline. Identify hub connectors at major studios, agencies, platforms, and organizations to help recruit attendees, and track progress against those targets throughout the invitation period, not just at the finish line.

Systems & Reporting

  • Own the CRM and audience database as a strategic system. Move the function off ad hoc tools and onto an integrated platform that supports registration, segmentation, and year-round relationship tracking, and tag attendees by role, influence, funder relationship, fellowship potential, dietary restrictions, and special needs so the data serves more than one event cycle.
  • Design a multi-stakeholder reporting structure. Build dashboards and metrics that translate raw audience data into clear, digestible insights for the Executive Director, funders, and cross-functional teams, so different stakeholders can see exactly what they need without you rebuilding the reporting each time.
  • Maintain live tracking and report progress on a set cadence. Keep a single master tracker covering RSVP health, room mix, VIP allocation, and flake rates, and report against goals in a weekly check-in with the Executive Director and cross-functional partners (Talent, Editorial, Fellowships, Fundraising) so the room is built deliberately over time, not assembled in a last-minute push.
  • Serve as the senior owner of cross-functional audience alignment. Define how the Audience & Community function interfaces with Talent, Editorial, Fundraising, Fellowships, and Production so audience decisions are explicitly tied to broader program goals, operating within clear guardrails and decision rights rather than relying on constant escalation.
  • Define and track outcome KPIs, not just operational metrics. Set targets for guest satisfaction, repeat engagement, and year-over-year retention, and report progress against them alongside room mix and RSVP data.
  • Track year-round community health. You are measuring participation across Evenings, fellowships, editorial engagement, repeat attendance, introductions made, and other indicators of long-term relationship growth—not just annual event attendance.
  • Run structured, proactive workflows. Build and manage the outreach calendar, invitation workflows, and templates for each audience segment, including the review and approval timeline across key stakeholders so materials move through sign-off without stalling, and independently hit deadlines and turnaround times without needing to be chased or have work taken over.
  • Own the working relationship with the graphic designer for audience-facing communications. Brief the designer directly on invitations, templates, and outreach materials, manage revisions and turnaround, and bring finished assets to the Executive Director for approval rather than routing every step through her.

Guest Experience & Day-of Operations

  • Bridge audience development and the day-of guest experience. Design the full guest journey from first invitation through on-site arrival, seating, and departure, working directly with production and logistics so the invitation process and hospitality experience feel like one seamless continuum rather than separate tracks.
  • Develop the audience logistics packet and manage partner fulfillment. Ensure funders, speakers, co-chairs, and key partners have their guests properly accommodated, from invitations and registration through on-site hospitality and special requests.
  • Own day-of audience operations. Lead registration and check-in protocols, VIP and priority guest handling, real-time seating and room-fill management, and serve as the final decision maker on live audience issues throughout the event.

Post-Event & Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Lead post-event learning and long-term relationship building. Manage the distribution and analysis of post-event audience surveys, capture structured feedback and impact data, report key insights to leadership and funders, and build a thoughtful, tiered follow-up strategy that connects attendees to fellowships, Evenings, future convenings, and other opportunities for continued engagement.
  • Develop and execute a year-round audience engagement calendar: that includes editorial updates, digital briefings, community check-ins, and opportunities for members to contribute to UC research, storytelling, fellowships, and future programming.
  • Build and steward a curated network of "UC Friendlies": trusted writers, creators, executives, researchers, philanthropists, and cultural leaders who can be activated throughout the year as contributors, moderators, hosts, advisors, speakers, fellowship participants, or connectors into new communities.

What You Bring

  • 8–10+ years in audience development, community strategy, membership, partnerships, or relationship-driven leadership roles in media, entertainment, philanthropy, or live experiences, with a demonstrated track record of building and stewarding communities and networks over time.
  • Demonstrated success building and activating communities over time—not simply managing audiences for individual events with the ability to turn participants into long-term collaborators, contributors, and ambassadors.
  • Senior enough to hold real decision-making authority across both audience development (strategy, curation, invitations) and audience management (hospitality, guest experience), managing them as one cohesive function rather than two disconnected tracks.
  • Deep knowledge of the entertainment and social-impact ecosystem, with genuine relationships across television, film, digital media, agencies, studios, philanthropy, nonprofits, advocacy organizations, and other culture-shaping communities.
  • Excellent judgment and creative instincts for audience curation. You know how to preserve trusted relationships while continually bringing new voices into the community, finding unconventional paths to the right room instead of relying on the same invite list every year.
  • Experience integrating relationship management with hospitality operations, including VIP travel, guest communications, registration, seating, and on-site experience, so every interaction feels like part of one cohesive guest journey.
  • Hands-on experience building and owning a CRM or audience platform (such as Whova, Cvent, Swapcard, or Swoogo) as a year-round relationship management system, not simply an event registration tool.
  • Comfortable directing and briefing creative execution. You can brief a designer clearly, give useful feedback on drafts, and bring polished, on-brand materials forward for final approval rather than requiring hands-on creative direction from leadership at every step.
  • Exceptional systems thinker with strong project management instincts. You naturally build scalable workflows, trackers, reporting structures, and operating systems that make teams more effective.
  • Rigorous attention to detail and reporting discipline. You build and maintain accurate, structured tracking and reporting systems as a matter of habit, not an afterthought.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and proactively. You hit deadlines, manage your own communications cadence, and drive work forward without needing to be pushed or having projects taken over.
  • Comfortable owning ambiguity and defining scope. You can build a new function and establish its guardrails rather than waiting for detailed direction.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills for funder-facing reporting, VIP correspondence, and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Able to work in an intensive event environment. The weeks leading into the convening require significant focus and availability, and major personal travel should be planned outside this period.
  • Must be able to be on-site in Los Angeles for event pre-production and the convening (April 4–6).

jobs.description:
Location: Remote

Reports to: Global Program Manager

Duration: 6 months

Time Commitment: This is a project-based position with defined deliverables; time commitment per week during the 6 month duration may vary.

Organization Overview

The Elba Hope Foundation is a nonprofit organization. At our heart lies a steadfast commitment to sustainable progress and better futures for Africans and the African Diaspora through the interconnected tools of agriculture, conservation, food security, education, youth advocacy, and social justice. Our mission is to drive transformative change by fostering innovation, empowering communities, and forming strategic partnerships that will have a lasting impact on these sectors, both today and for future generations.

Position Overview

The Elba Hope Foundation is seeking a Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) Advisor to strengthen the organization’s approach to program monitoring, performance measurement, learning, and reporting across programs in the United Kingdom (UK), Sierra Leone (SL), and the United States (US). The Advisor will develop a practical, harmonized MEAL framework that supports consistent measurement across the organization while allowing for appropriate adaptation to each country and program context. A core focus of the assignment will be to establish the plans, tools, workflows, and systems required for continued monitoring beyond the consultancy period.

Key Responsibilities

The Advisor will work with relevant program and leadership teams to:

  • Develop MEAL plans and frameworks for each program.
  • Define appropriate indicators, data sources, collection methods, responsibilities, and reporting schedules.
  • Develop standardized and context-specific monitoring and data collection tools.
  • Establish workflows and systems for routine collection, validation, analysis, reporting, and use of program data.
  • Strengthen organizational capacity to maintain and use the MEAL system on an ongoing basis.
  • Support staff training, documentation, and handover to ensure sustainability after the consultancy ends.

Qualifications

The preferred consultant should demonstrate:

  • Significant professional experience in monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning.
  • Experience designing organizational or multi-program MEAL systems.
  • Demonstrated experience developing MEAL plans, indicators, data collection tools, and reporting frameworks.
  • Experience building monitoring workflows and sustainable data management processes.
  • Strong understanding of quantitative and qualitative monitoring methods.
  • Experience supporting programs operating across multiple countries or contexts.
  • Ability to translate technical MEAL concepts into practical tools for program staff.
  • Experience delivering staff training and capacity building.
  • Strong analytical, facilitation, and technical writing skills.

Experience working with global programs, or comparable contexts is desirable.

Deliverables

The consultancy will result in a practical, proportionate, and sustainable MEAL system that EHF staff can operate and maintain using existing organizational capacity and Google Workspace.

The Advisor will develop one common EHF MEAL architecture, with program-specific adaptations where required for Hope Power Project, Creative Futures, and DYSF. The Advisor is expected to build on existing systems and materials wherever practical rather than recreate tools or processes that are already fit for purpose.The total fixed professional fee for satisfactory completion of the scope is USD$28,000, payable upon EHF's acceptance of the following deliverables:

  1. Contract Execution & Approved Workplan: Finalized contract; kickoff meeting; agreed methodology, workplan, consultation schedule, and document/data request.
  2. MEAL Diagnostic & Implementation Priorities: Focused assessment of existing MEAL practices, tools, data, partner reporting, prior research, and staff capacity across the three programs; identification of gaps and assets that can be retained; prioritized recommendations for system development.
  3. EHF Organizational MEAL Framework & Master Indicator Framework: One common EHF results and measurement architecture; manageable organizational and program indicator set; indicator definitions, data sources, collection frequencies, responsibilities, quality standards, reporting expectations, and approach to learning and adaptation.
  4. Program MEAL Plans: Operational measurement plans/matrices focused on Hope Power Project, with lighter engagements for Creative Futures and DYSF. Creative Futures includes practical longer-term tracking of skills, confidence, and employment outcomes; DYSF includes media, awareness, advocacy, event, and public/policy engagement measures; Hope Power receives the greatest technical depth across electricity, digital access/skills, education/employment, livelihoods/economic outcomes, and agricultural training.
  5. MEAL Toolkit & Accountability Tools: Standardized data-collection and reporting templates; partner reporting tools; participant feedback and outcome tools; longitudinal follow-up tools where appropriate; data-quality checks; learning/reflection templates; and necessary Hope Power-specific tools. Includes a formal, proportionate Hope Power community feedback and complaints-response mechanism.
  6. EHF Data Workflow & MEAL SOPs: Practical organization-wide workflow covering data collection/receipt, partner submission, validation, entry, storage, review, reporting, escalation, learning, and use. Concise MEAL SOP documenting roles, responsibilities, procedures, quality controls, and system maintenance.
  7. Google Sheets Performance Tracking System & Dashboard: Operational Google Sheets-based single source of truth for approved EHF program metrics; standardized data structures; program and organizational views; targets and actuals where appropriate; automated summaries/charts; validation controls; and instructions for routine updating and maintenance. EHF will prepare requested historical data for import.
  8. Staff Training & System Launch: Practical training for EHF staff who will enter, validate, manage, or use MEAL data to confirm that staff understand indicators, tools, workflow, quality requirements, dashboard use, accountability processes, and routine system maintenance.
  9. Live Pilot, Refinement & Final Handover: Support for one live reporting and data-collection cycle; assessment of usability, data quality, indicator clarity, workflow, and dashboard performance; reasonable refinements based on pilot findings; complete final package of approved materials; implementation / maintenance roadmap; final handover meeting.

Scope Parameters

The USD $28,000 fixed fee assumes a proportionate system designed for EHF's current organizational scale and operating model.

The scope assumes:

  • Three core programs: Hope Power Project, Creative Futures, and DSYF with the majority of the Advisor’s focus on the more complex Hope Power Project.
  • Creative Futures UK and emerging US delivery will use one common program MEAL approach, with limited geographic adaptations made by program staff where genuinely necessary.
  • Google Sheets will be the primary performance-tracking technology.
  • EHF will prepare historical data for migration in an agreed format.
  • The Advisor will design data-collection and assessment methodologies but will not conduct large-scale primary research, baseline studies, or impact evaluations.
  • The Advisor will support one live system pilot/reporting cycle.
  • The system will be designed for semiannual organizational performance review while allowing program data to be updated at appropriate intervals.

Benefits

  • Flexible remote work environment.
  • Opportunity to support sustainable and accountable M&E for a growing global nonprofit.
  • Collaborative, mission-driven team with meaningful international impact.

Application Instructions

Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter describing your experience and fit for the role. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

We are seeking candidates who bring a deep contextual understanding of Africa and a strong alignment with our mission and values. This may come through lived experience, long-term professional engagement, or meaningful personal connection to the regions and communities we serve. Our work is rooted in respect for local leadership, cultural knowledge, and community-driven solutions, and we prioritize applicants who demonstrate humility, accountability, and a clear commitment to working in partnership with diverse stakeholders.

The Elba Hope Foundation is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.

Salary: USD $28,000 flat fee

Location: Remote (based in Estonia)

Contract: 12 months, full-time, service agreement.

Nidus Balticus is looking for an entrepreneurial and proactive Country Representative to lead and grow our work in Estonia.

This is a highly autonomous role with significant ownership of Nidus Balticus’ strategic delivery in Estonia. You will implement Nidus Balticus’ country strategy, developing programmes, partnerships and policy initiatives that advance our strategic objectives. One priority will be leading the next phase of our work in Ida-Virumaa – strengthening its political and policy impact, developing partnerships around regional priorities, and connecting local priorities with national political and investment decisions. Beyond Ida-Virumaa, you will be expected to identify and develop new programme and partnership opportunities, expand our ecosystem of collaborators, and contribute to shaping Nidus Balticus’ broader policy and campaign agenda in Estonia. As our presence grows, you will build a local team.

You will report directly to the Executive Director and collaborate closely with the Chief Operations Officer, PR Manager, and other Country Leads.

About Nidus Balticus

Nidus Balticus is a non-profit organization working to strengthen energy independence, environmental stewardship, and national security across the Baltics. We bring underrepresented voices into energy and environmental policy conversations, building broad coalitions that connect local communities, civil society, businesses, and policymakers. By turning community engagement into public support, we help create the political momentum needed to deliver lasting policy change.

Nidus Balticus is part of Our Common Home (OCH) – a global network that brings those excluded from the climate movement into the conversation about protecting their environment, on their own terms. Our 10+ network organizations are active across four continents, supported by a global team providing world-class expertise in campaigns, impact measurement, research, and operations.

Key Responsibilities

Country strategy & strategic delivery: Lead the implementation of Nidus Balticus’ Estonia strategy, translating strategic priorities into programmes, campaigns, partnerships and policy initiatives. Identify opportunities to expand our impact and strengthen our presence in Estonia, and take ownership of new initiatives.

Programme development & delivery: Design, launch and deliver strategic campaigns and programmes, including the continued development of our flagship work in Ida-Virumaa. Oversee implementation, coordinate local partners and vendors, manage budgets and timelines, and ensure programmes achieve societal and policy impact.

Partnerships & ecosystem development: Build and nurture an ecosystem of partners across civil society, business, academia, municipalities, and government. Establish strategic partnerships and alliances that strengthen impact, policy influence, and programme delivery.

New opportunities & partnerships: Continuously identify and develop new programme, campaign and partnership opportunities aligned with the mission and country strategy. Identify emerging political and societal needs, assess opportunities for Nidus Balticus to create impact, and turn relevant opportunities into concrete initiatives.

Policy engagement: Build relationships with policymakers and public institutions, contribute to policy discussions, and support our advocacy work in Estonia.

Leadership & team development: Help establish and grow Nidus Balticus' presence in Estonia by identifying future talent, supporting recruitment, and gradually building and leading a high-performing local team.

Public representation: Represent Nidus Balticus at conferences, public events, stakeholder meetings, and in regional media.

Impact & reporting: Monitor programme impact, gather community insights, and contribute to reports, case studies, and learning processes.

Requirements

Experience: 5–8+ years of relevant professional experience in public affairs, advocacy, strategic partnerships, regional development, programme development, community engagement, or ecosystem building, ideally with ownership of complex initiatives or organisational growth.

Stakeholder engagement: Demonstrated ability to build trusted partnerships across different sectors and work effectively with diverse communities.

Ecosystem building: Proven ability to develop multi-stakeholder partnerships and build collaborative ecosystems involving civil society, businesses, public institutions, and local communities.

Regional expertise: Good understanding of Estonia's political, social, and economic landscape. Familiarity with Ida-Virumaa and existing networks in the region would be a strong advantage.

Languages: Fluency in Estonian and English is essential. Russian language skills are highly desirable for engaging diverse communities and stakeholders.

Organization: Strong project management skills with the ability to independently coordinate multiple workstreams.

Communication: Excellent interpersonal and public speaking skills, with the ability to build trust across diverse audiences.

Entrepreneurial mindset: High degree of ownership, autonomy and initiative. Proactively identifies opportunities, is comfortable operating with ambiguity, and can take an initiative from an early opportunity through relationship-building, programme development and implementation.

Who is the Ideal Candidate?

Relevant backgrounds may include:

Community development & NGOs: Experience leading outreach, mobilization, or partnership-building within civil society or community projects.

Public affairs & advocacy: Experience engaging policymakers, public institutions, or industry stakeholders on policy or advocacy initiatives.

Business & industry associations: Experience working within chambers of commerce, business associations, sector organizations, employers' associations, or regional development bodies, bringing stakeholders together around shared policy objectives.

Ecosystem building & strategic partnerships: A proven track record of building cross-sector partnerships between NGOs, businesses, public institutions, research organisations, foundations, or community groups.

Regional development: Experience working with municipalities, local development organizations, regional initiatives, or place-based economic development.

Project management: Experience coordinating initiatives involving multiple partners, timelines, and deliverables.

What We Offer

Autonomy: High degree of freedom in planning and executing your work.

Leadership Opportunity: Shape Nidus Balticus' long-term presence in Estonia, implement the country's strategic vision, and build and lead an agile and ambitiouslocal team.

Meaningful Impact: The opportunity to play a leading role in strengthening communities, building broad societal coalitions, and advancing Estonia's long-term energy security and regional resilience.

Competitive Compensation:

Flexibility: Remote working conditions within an agile, modern organizational culture.

International Network: Learning and networking opportunities within Our Common Home's global network.

Contract: An initial 12-month fixed-term contract, with a strong potential for extension as the organization expands.

Travel: Regular travel within Estonia, particularly to regional communities, and occasional travel across the Baltics for meetings and collaboration.

Looking for Philippines-based candidates

Job Role: SEO Specialist

Engagement type:Independent Contractor Agreement

Who We Are: At Hunt St, we help Australian companies hire top remote talent in the Philippines. For this role, you will be engaged directly by the client as an independent contractor. We are not an outsourcing agency. All of our roles are 100% remote so you'll be able to work from home.

Who The Client Is: Our client is an established Australian digital marketing agency supporting businesses with end-to-end digital solutions designed to improve their online presence, generate leads, and achieve measurable business outcomes.

The agency works across a broad range of digital services, combining creative, technical, and performance-focused expertise to deliver tailored solutions for its clients. Their team takes a results-driven approach, with a strong focus on transparency, quality, collaboration, and long-term client relationships.

Role Overview: We are hiring a senior, AI enabled SEO specialist to work alongside our Australian staff, not underneath them. You will own SEO delivery across a portfolio of client sites end to end: audit, plan, execute, report.

The AI part is not a buzzword on the ad. It is how we expect the work to get done. Search itself is changing, with AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini now sitting between our clients and their customers, and the way SEO work is produced is changing just as fast. We want someone who already uses AI daily to do the work of a much larger team, and who has the judgement to know when the AI is wrong.

This is a hands-on role for someone who has already run their own client book and does not need daily direction. If you need a task list handed to you each morning, this is not the one.

You will report directly to the Head of SEO, in Perth. The Philippines and Perth share the same timezone (UTC+8), so you are on the same clock as the team. No split shift and no overnight work.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own on page and technical SEO across a portfolio of roughly 10 to 20 client WordPress sites
  • Run technical audits and fix what you find: crawl issues, indexation, redirects, site structure, Core Web Vitals, schema
  • Optimise for AI search as well as Google. Structure content and schema so clients get cited in AI Overviews and LLM answers, and track where they are appearing
  • Use AI to scale the work: research, clustering, brief generation, first draft copy, bulk meta data, audit summarisation, report commentary, with a human check before anything ships
  • Build and improve repeatable AI workflows for the team, so a task done well once gets done fast every time after
  • Keyword research and content briefs mapped to client services and commercial intent
  • Write and optimise page copy, meta data and blog content to a standard that reads human, never generic
  • Google Business Profile optimisation and local SEO for WA service area businesses
  • Build monthly client reports in Looker Studio that explain what changed and why, not just charts
  • Monitor rankings, traffic and conversions, and flag drops before the client does
  • Migration QA: pre launch SEO checks, redirect maps, post launch verification
  • Work with our developers on implementation, and QA it once it is live
  • Bring recommendations to the Head of SEO and the Perth team proactively. We want a second brain, not a pair of hands

Requirements

  • 5+ years in SEO, with at least 2 in an agency managing multiple client accounts at once
  • Demonstrable daily use of AI tools in real SEO delivery (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or similar). They can show us workflows they have built, not just tools they have tried
  • Editorial judgement over AI output. They know what AI generated content sounds like and they do not let it out the door. Clients get work that reads like a person wrote it, because they rewrote it
  • Working understanding of AI search: how AI Overviews and LLM answers pick sources, and what to change on a site to be one of them
  • Genuine technical SEO capability. They can read a crawl report, diagnose the cause and specify the fix
  • Strong WordPress experience: Yoast or RankMath, page builders, plugin level troubleshooting
  • Google Search Console, GA4 and Looker Studio to a reporting ready standard
  • Screaming Frog or equivalent, and SEMrush or Ahrefs, used daily rather than occasionally
  • Excellent written English. They will write client facing copy and reports that go out with our name on them
  • Able to work independently across a portfolio and manage their own priorities
  • Reliable home office setup and stable internet, available 8:00am to 4:00pm AWST

NICE TO HAVE SKILLS

  • Automation platforms such as n8n, Make or Zapier, for connecting SEO tasks, data and reporting
  • Custom GPTs, Claude Projects, or their own prompt library built for repeat client work
  • Light scripting in Python or Apps Script, including AI assisted, for bulk data work and API pulls
  • HTML and CSS literacy, enough to diagnose and make small front end fixes themselves
  • Cloudflare, GTM or Zaraz, or server side tagging exposure WooCommerce or e-commerce SEO
  • Google Ads familiarity, enough to see where paid and organic overlap
  • Experience mentoring or QA'ing junior SEO work
  • Australian market experience, or a track record with English speaking Western clients

IDEAL CANDIDATE PROFILE

  • Someone senior enough to be trusted with client outcomes and steady enough to still be here in three years.
  • AI native, not AI dependent. Uses AI to move faster on everything, and still owns every word that ships
  • Independent. Runs their own week, chases their own loose ends, escalates early when something is off
  • Diagnostic. Does not just report that traffic dropped. Finds out why and proposes the fix
  • Curious about the shift. Search is being rebuilt right now and we want someone who finds that interesting rather than threatening
  • Communicative. Writes clearly, updates without being asked, comfortable saying "that recommendation will not work, here is why"
  • Long term. We are building a role, not filling a gap. Growth into leading SEO delivery alongside the Head of SEO as the client base grows is on the table

Work Arrangement & Expectations:

This is a remote role that will be set up as an independent contractor engagement.

To ensure alignment and transparency, successful candidates will be expected to:

  • Disclose any existing ongoing roles or client work
  • Reflect this engagement on their LinkedIn profile (clearly marked as “Independent Contractor”)

jobs.excerpt: When the Tarr Steps, a footbridge assembled of heavy stones in Exmoor National Park in England, washed away in a flood in 1942, the Royal Engineers rebuilt it.
jobs.description:
When the Tarr Steps, a footbridge assembled of heavy stones in Exmoor National Park in England, washed away in a flood in 1942, the Royal Engineers rebuilt it. Then it washed away again in 1952. So the Royal Engineers heaved in more stones: on and on, like a Sisyphean lesson in absurdity.

Of course, they do this because the Tarr Steps are a historical monument, believed to be built during the Bronze Age. Modern bridge building looks a lot different and generally requires less upkeep. While we appreciate the charm of ancient things, Mercury is engineering the future of banking*. "Quaint" and "archaic" are not values we seek in our systems. Rebooting a tumbling server and hoping a flood of requests doesn't wash it away can be an emergency tactic, but we actively seek out durable solutions over monotonous ops work. You'll bring this ethos and teach others how to live it too.

Up to this point, the Stability team at Mercury has primarily built platform-level constructs that product teams adopt. However, those teams are asking for us to work more closely with them to mature their implementations and practices. We are creating an SRE team that will rotate through product teams. You will understand the team's domain, identify opportunities for improvements in reliability/observability/performance/preparedness and create self-reinforcing, virtuous cycles.

As part of this role, you will:

  • Embed with product teams, helping them improve their operational maturity by setting up and refining practices around on-call, monitoring, alerting, and run books
  • Run regular game day exercises with product teams, helping them feel more prepared to investigate and quickly remediate incidents
  • Jump into application code written in Haskell & TypeScript and implement reliability techniques such as retries, better error handling, better logging, circuit breaking, etc
  • Steer SLOs towards meaningful customer outcomes that product teams are accountable for. Those SLOs become a strong signal for whether the product is working as intended
  • Champion reliability practices through design document and code reviews
  • Identify observability gaps that hinder debugging, incident response, and business intelligence and help close those
  • Advocate for longer-term improvements that non-product engineering teams can drive
  • Participate in the product team's on-call rotation while embedding or as part of a more general engineering rotation, helping us improve processes and how we learn from incidents

The ideal candidate for the role:

  • Has past Site Reliability Engineering or DevOps experience
  • Has measurable examples of influencing an organization towards greater reliability
  • Has significant experience with PostgreSQL
  • Has authored and operated Temporal workflows
  • Has experience with observability platforms like Grafana or Honeycomb
  • Has familiarity with OpenTelemetry

Perform monitoring and site management work to ensure that sites are conducting the study(ies) and reporting study data as required by the study protocol, applicable regulations and guidelines, and sponsor requirements.

Essential Functions
• Perform site monitoring visits (selection, initiation, monitoring and close-out visits) in accordance with contracted scope of work and Good Clinical Practice.

• Administer protocol and related study training to assigned sites and establish regular lines of communication with sites to manage ongoing project expectations and issues.
• Evaluate the quality and integrity of study site practices related to the proper conduct of the protocol and adherence to applicable regulations. Escalate quality issues as appropriate.

• Create and maintain appropriate documentation regarding site management, monitoring visit findings and action plans by submitting regular visit reports, generating follow-up letters and other required study documentation.
• Collaborate and liaise with study team members for project execution support as appropriate.
• If applicable, may be accountable for supporting development of project subject recruitment plan on a per site basis.
• If applicable, may be accountable for site financial management according to executed clinical trial agreement and retrieve invoices according to local requirement.

Qualifications
• Bachelor's Degree Degree in scientific discipline or health care preferred. Req

• Good knowledge of, and skill in applying, applicable clinical research regulatory requirements.

• Computer skills including proficiency in use of Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint and use of a laptop computer and iPhone and iPad (where applicable).

WEB DEVELOPER

Independent Contractor | Remote | Minimum 10 Hours/Week

This is an independent contractor (1099) position. VaVa contractors are responsible for managing their own taxes, benefits, and business expenses.

VaVa Virtual Assistants is a remote company based out of Atlanta, Georgia, built on the belief that businesses thrive when they have the right support behind them. We connect clients across industries like nonprofit, legal, coaching, and finance with skilled virtual professionals who bring genuine expertise to the work. Our team may be distributed, but the culture is deeply connected through daily conversation, project collaboration, and regular all-company virtual gatherings.

We are looking for an experienced Web Developer who is already freelancing or running their own web development practice and wants to supplement that work with additional client projects through VaVa. This role calls for both front end and backend expertise, along with the technical range to move between quick maintenance requests, full site builds, and ecommerce or security work as each project demands.

Beyond your client work, you will be part of a contractor community that genuinely invests in one another's success. Regular calls with clients and fellow contractors keep you connected to the broader VaVa team, and every interaction is an opportunity to reflect our mission, vision, and values.

Please review the requirements and qualifications below carefully, as they reflect what it truly takes to succeed in this role. We appreciate your interest in joining the team.

EXPECTATIONS

Represent VaVa Virtual Assistants in a Positive and Professional Manner

  • Demonstrate strong technical judgment and professionalism in every client interaction.
  • Ensure all communication reflects VaVa's values and standard of quality.
  • Contribute to a collaborative culture among fellow VaVa contractors, including designers or other specialists who may support your projects.

Take Ownership of Client Satisfaction

  • Manage client website projects and ongoing support requests with reliability and follow-through.
  • Anticipate technical needs before they become urgent issues, and communicate proactively about progress and timelines.
  • Deliver work that meets each client's brand, functionality, and performance goals.
  • Adjust availability and scope as project demands shift, from routine maintenance to full site builds or migrations.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Design, develop, and maintain websites for multiple clients across a range of industries, primarily using WordPress.
  • Build and customize front end interfaces using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript that align with each client's brand and goals.
  • Develop, troubleshoot, and maintain backend functionality using PHP, resolving issues promptly to minimize downtime and disruption to client business.
  • Manage e-commerce site builds and ongoing maintenance on platforms such as WooCommerce, Shopify, or ThriveCart.
  • Execute website migrations, domain transfers, and hosting changes with minimal disruption to client operations.
  • Configure and maintain website security measures to protect client sites from vulnerabilities, downtime, and unauthorized access.
  • Build landing pages and set up automations and system integrations, using tools such as Zapier, Make, or n8n, and email marketing platforms such as ConvertKit or Klaviyo, when a client's project calls for it.
  • Monitor website analytics and traffic, and optimize client sites for search engines and answer engines using current SEO and AEO practices, reporting on client-defined performance metrics.
  • Use AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT to support development work, troubleshoot issues, and build custom workflows for clients, staying current on emerging web development tools and AI-assisted practices.
  • Collaborate with designers, including VaVa contractors supporting brand, graphic design, or content writing needs, when a project calls for additional creative support.
  • Gather and refine project requirements directly from clients, and communicate timelines, progress, and technical concepts in accessible, non-technical language.
  • Provide ongoing maintenance and ad hoc support for existing client sites, managing multiple concurrent projects and balancing routine work with new builds and migrations.
  • Maintain clear documentation of site structure, credentials, and technical decisions for each client project.
  • Complete additional web development tasks as requested, within the scope of the contractor engagement.

GENERAL QUALIFICATIONS

  • Must reside and be authorized to work in the United States.
  • At least 3 years of demonstrated experience in front end and backend web development.
  • At least 2 years of experience working full-time in a virtual or remote capacity.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting multiple clients across different industries; candidates who are actively running their own web development practice or taking on independent freelance engagements are strongly preferred.
  • Available a minimum of 10 hours per week, with flexibility to take on additional ad hoc client projects as they arise.

TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS

Must Have

  • Proficiency in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with backend development experience in PHP.
  • Proficiency in WordPress, including theme customization, plugin management, site migrations, and troubleshooting, along with experience on at least one ecommerce platform such as WooCommerce, Shopify, or ThriveCart.
  • Experience with SEO and answer engine optimization (AEO), including Google Analytics, Search Console, and Tag Manager.
  • Experience with automation and systems integration tools such as Zapier, Make, or n8n, and email marketing or landing page platforms such as ConvertKit or Klaviyo.
  • Experience implementing website security best practices to protect client sites from vulnerabilities and downtime.
  • AI literacy, including experience using tools such as Claude or ChatGPT to support development work and improve workflow efficiency.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, Slack, and Zoom.
  • Experience with at least one project management tool and one CRM tool.

Preferred

  • Experience with alternate website builder platforms such as Webflow, Wix, or Squarespace, or with AI-assisted builders such as Showit, Loveable, or Durable.
  • Graphic design and UX/UI experience, including wireframing in Figma or Adobe Illustrator.
  • Familiarity with Git/GitHub, SQL, or Python.

EDUCATION

A degree is not required. Demonstrated competency and a strong portfolio of front end work always outweigh credentials.

A degree or certificate in web development, computer science, or a related field is a plus, but not required.

Candidates without a degree should hold at least one relevant certification. Examples include: WordPress certification, AWS Certified Developer, a Google Analytics certification, or a foundational security certification like CompTIA Security+.

A commitment to continued learning is an expectation of this role. New technology and software capabilities shift regularly; staying current is part of the job.

jobs.title: Director of Communications & Content
jobs.excerpt: Company Overview Agility PR Solutions is a global leader in media intelligence and PR technology.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Agility PR Solutions is a global leader in media intelligence and PR technology. Founded in 2003, we help communications teams around the world drive awareness, make smarter decisions, and protect their reputation when it matters most. Our enterprise-grade platform unifies media relations, media monitoring, social listening, AI visibility, and media intelligence into a single seamless system—turning overwhelming streams of coverage and conversation into decision-ready intelligence. Recognized for ease of use, results, and customer support, Agility is one of the most trusted names in media intelligence. Our mission is to empower the voices that shape the world's narratives, and we're looking for people who want to help us do it.

About the Role

Reporting to the VP of Marketing, the Director of Communications & Content is Agility's editorial and communications leader: editor-in-chief of Bulldog Reporter, owner of our flagship research properties, and head of Agility's own earned media and PR program. This role requires a rare combination — a genuine PR or editorial background paired with real content marketing experience — and both are essential.

Bulldog Reporter is your publication. The mandate is a turnaround: grow the audience from roughly 5,000 active subscribers to 20,000 within 12 months at disciplined acquisition economics, through six established editorial franchise formats. The publication's operating principle is journalism first — credible, useful reporting for PR professionals — with our platform as its instrument. You set and defend the editorial standard, direct the franchise strategy, arbitrate the production queue between editorial and campaign demands, and own the Bulldog Awards program, whose credibility rests on the same editorial integrity as the publication itself.

You own both of our flagship research properties — our primary research on the true cost of manual reporting, and our study of the gap between how brands think they appear in AI-generated answers and how they actually do. Both are built from a single field instrument you will design: survey construction, methodology, analysis, and the reports themselves. You will defend the methodology publicly, because these reports are built to be cited.

You run everything earned. A company that sells PR software must be excellent at its own PR: press outreach, analyst and media relations, industry awards, and executive visibility all belong to you, alongside our thought-leader program.

You will manage the Content Marketing Manager — and help hire them, which is why this role is filled first — and you will collaborate closely with the Associate Director, Demand Generation, since a substantial share of the content organization's output serves demand campaigns.

What Success Looks Like

  • Bulldog Reporter grows from approximately 5,000 to 20,000 active subscribers within 12 months, at or below target acquisition cost, with engagement quality holding as the list scales.
  • Both flagship research reports ship on schedule with defensible methodology, earning measurable coverage, citations, and derivative content.
  • Agility's earned media program is visibly alive: consistent press coverage, working analyst relationships, award wins, and executive visibility for company leadership.
  • The editorial standard holds across the publication and the content organization's output — a consistent, recognizable house register without drift.
  • The Content Marketing Manager is hired, developed, and productive, with the production queue arbitrated so both editorial and campaign content ship.
  • Content performance is reviewed on a regular numbers cadence, and what works is identified, understood, and built upon.

What you’ll do

Bulldog Reporter — Editor-in-Chief

  • Own audience growth strategy and its economics; direct the six editorial franchise formats.
  • Set and enforce the editorial standard; edit hard and develop the writers you edit.
  • Arbitrate the production queue between editorial franchises and campaign content needs.
  • Direct the contributor network through the Content Marketing Manager.
  • Own the Bulldog Awards program — categories, judging standards, and the editorial integrity that makes the recognition worth winning — with field marketing running live ceremony mechanics and community activation of entrants.

Flagship Research

  • Design the field instrument: survey construction, sampling, and methodology.
  • Direct analysis and author the flagship reports; own their quality and their launch narratives.
  • Defend the methodology publicly with press, analysts, and practitioners.
  • Partner with field marketing, which produces the launch webinars and readout events that put the research on stage.

Earned Media & PR Program

  • Run Agility's press outreach, analyst and media relations, and awards program.
  • Build executive visibility for company leadership through speaking, bylines, and interviews.
  • Direct the thought-leader program.
  • Engage agency or freelance support where it genuinely accelerates outcomes.

Team & Editorial Leadership

  • Hire, manage, and develop the Content Marketing Manager.
  • Take briefs from — and negotiate priorities with — the Associate Director, Demand Generation.
  • Internalize how the platform works so the publication's journalism-first, platform-as-instrument framing is executed with integrity.
  • Review content performance data on a weekly cadence and turn learnings into the next assignment.

What You'll Bring

  • A genuine PR or editorial background — newsroom experience or communications leadership — combined with hands-on content marketing experience. Both are required.
  • Experience building research reports: instrument design, survey execution, analysis, and methodology you were willing to defend in public.
  • Audience or newsletter growth experience with numbers you can show, strongly preferred.
  • A head for numbers: highly analytical, outcome-driven, and fluent in content performance data.
  • Business savvy and strategic judgment — you connect editorial decisions to commercial outcomes without corrupting the journalism.
  • People leadership experience, and the collaborative instincts to work daily with a demand generation counterpart.
  • A sense of urgency and a test-and-learn mindset: when a piece works, you ask why, and you build on it.
  • Fluency in the PR and communications industry and its practitioners — our readers and our buyers.

Why You'll Love It Here

  • Fully remote work environment
  • Collaborative culture – and key tools enabling it
  • Competitive compensation package
  • Health, Dental & Vision benefits
  • RRSP matching
  • Life Insurance
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Career Development & Progression opportunities
  • Paid Vacation, Personal Days and Sick days
  • Flex Fridays in Summer, Week off between Christmas and New Years'
  • No Internal Meetings Fridays

Compensation

The base salary range for this role is C$120,000–C$165,000 annually, plus a 15% target bonus. Final compensation will reflect the successful candidate's experience, skills, and internal equity.

This is a new position.

AI Usage

We use technology to make hiring smarter, faster, and more personal, never less human. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools help us manage applications efficiently and highlight qualifications that align with each role, allowing our recruiters to focus more on meaningful conversations with candidates. AI does not make hiring decisions at Agility. Every decision is made by people, our hiring managers and recruitment professionals, who are trained to apply sound judgment and equitable practices at every stage. We believe technology exists to amplify human insight, not replace it. That belief shapes how we build relationships, tell stories, and grow our teams.

At Agility, we strive every day to build a more inclusive work environment and introduce tools that enable it. We strongly encourage applications from all people regardless of race, religion, gender, age, disability status or sexual orientation.

Even if you find yourself not checking all the boxes of our listed requirements but you are excited about this opportunity, we'd love to hear from you anyway. Our Talent Acquisition team will review your application for this role, and other potential role matches open now or in the future.

If, at any stage of the application process, you require accommodation owing to disability or a medical need, please let us know at for us to make appropriate arrangements.
